title: Apple researchers find language discrimination improves multilingual speech models
excerpt: New interventions in pretraining reduce the performance gap between multilingual and monolingual speech models.
bodyHtml:
Apple researchers Maureen de Seyssel, Jie Chi, and Zakaria Aldeneh announced on October 2, 2026, that strengthening a model's ability to discriminate languages during pretraining reduces the performance gap between multilingual and monolingual speech models. The study utilized a controlled English and French HuBERT setting, a type of self-supervised speech model, to test the impact of language discrimination.

The researchers implemented two interventions: an auxiliary language classifier and per-language k-means targets. These methods resulted in a decrease in phone discrimination error from 11.6% in the bilingual baseline to 10.4%.

Lexical performance increased from 52.1% to 56.7%, and prosodic performance improved from 68.9% to 72.9%. The study found that the most significant gains occurred when language discrimination was introduced in the first iteration of training, while later or repeated interventions yielded smaller improvements.
topic: Language Discrimination Improves Linguistic Learning in Multilingual Speech Models
